stories.text: Amara Okafor sold tomatoes at the market in Enugu on Saturday morning. Her brother Chidi helped her carry three baskets from the farm. At noon a woman named Mrs. Bello bought two baskets for her restaurant. Amara gave the last basket to Chidi because he had worked so hard. He took it home to their mother.
qs: Who sold tomatoes at the market?
Who helped Amara carry the baskets?
How many baskets did Mrs. Bello buy?
Who did Chidi take the basket to?

stories.text: Kenji Watanabe repaired bicycles in a small shop near the train station. On Tuesday a girl named Yuki brought in a bike with a flat tire. Kenji patched the tire and oiled the chain. It took him forty minutes. Yuki paid him with coins from her pocket and rode off to school.
qs: When did Yuki bring in the bike?
Where did Yuki ride off to?

stories.text: A fox named Rusk lived at the edge of a birch forest. One cold evening he found a red mitten lying in the snow. He carried it to his den and slept on it all night. In the morning a squirrel called Pip came looking for the mitten, because she wanted to line her nest with it. Rusk gave the mitten to Pip, and she thanked him with a handful of acorns.
qs: What did Rusk find in the snow?
Where did Rusk carry the mitten?
Why did Pip want the mitten?
she wanted to line her nest with it

stories.text: Priya Sharma worked as a nurse at the city hospital in Pune. Her shift began at seven o'clock every morning. On Monday she met a new doctor, Dr. Rao, who had just arrived from Chennai. He asked Priya where the supply room was. She walked him down the hall and showed him the door.
qs: Who had just arrived from Chennai?
Where had Dr. Rao arrived from?

stories.text: Elena and her grandfather Tomas went fishing on the lake early on Sunday. They rowed a green boat to the middle of the water. Tomas caught four fish, but Elena caught only one. She was not sad, because her fish was the biggest. They cooked the fish for lunch at the cabin.
qs: How many fish did Tomas catch?
Where did they cook the fish?

stories.text: Mr. Haddad owned a bakery on Cedar Street. Every Friday he baked fifty loaves of bread before dawn. His daughter Leila sold the bread at the front counter. One Friday the oven broke, so Mr. Haddad called a repairman named Omar. Omar fixed the oven by noon, and the bakery opened late.

Sipho kept a goat named Bina on his family's farm. Bina liked to climb onto the roof of the shed. On Wednesday afternoon she jumped from the roof into the vegetable garden and ate the cabbages. Sipho's mother was angry and built a taller fence. After that, Bina stayed in the field behind the house.
qs: Where did Bina stay after that?
in the field behind the house

stories.text: Ingrid Larsen took the night train from Oslo to Bergen. She shared a cabin with an old man who was reading a newspaper. He told her that his name was Olav and that he was going to visit his son. In the morning Olav left his umbrella on the seat. Ingrid ran after him on the platform and handed it back.
qs: Who was Olav going to visit?
What did Olav leave on the seat?

stories.text: The village of Santa Rita held a fair every spring. This year Miguel brought his best pig, and his cousin Rosa brought a basket of honey. A judge in a straw hat gave Rosa a blue ribbon for her honey. Miguel's pig won nothing, but he sold it to a farmer for twenty dollars. That evening the whole village danced in the square.
qs: Who brought a basket of honey?
What did the judge give Rosa?
Who did Miguel sell the pig to?

stories.text: Hana Kim was a student at Pine Hill School. On Thursday her teacher, Mr. Lee, asked the class to write a poem about the sea. Hana wrote about a whale that sang to the moon. Mr. Lee liked it so much that he read it aloud to the class. Later Hana gave a copy of the poem to her friend Jun.
qs: Who was a student at Pine Hill School?
What did Mr. Lee ask the class to write?
When did Mr. Lee ask the class to write?
Who got a copy of the poem?

stories.text: A storm hit the coastal town of Port Mary on Saturday night. The wind blew the roof off Mrs. Grant's chicken coop. Her neighbor, Ben Ashford, came over on Sunday with a hammer and a box of nails. Together they put the roof back on in two hours. Mrs. Grant thanked Ben with a dozen eggs.
qs: the coastal town of port mary
Whose chicken coop lost its roof?
Who came over with a hammer?
What did Mrs. Grant give Ben?

stories.text: Tariq worked at a bookshop in Cairo. One morning an old woman came in looking for a book about birds. Tariq found it on the top shelf and climbed a ladder to reach it. The woman paid with a large note, and Tariq gave her change. She put the book in her bag and walked toward the river.
qs: What was the old woman looking for?
Where did Tariq find the book?

stories.text: Lucia and Marco Bianchi were twins who lived above their parents' restaurant in Naples. Every evening Lucia set the tables and Marco washed the glasses. On Saturday a famous singer came to dinner. Marco was so nervous that he dropped a tray of glasses. The singer laughed and signed Lucia's notebook.
qs: above their parents' restaurant in naples
Whose notebook did the singer sign?

stories.text: An old turtle named Gorm lived in a pond behind the church. Every summer the children of the village came to feed him lettuce. One year a boy named Felix noticed that Gorm had a crack in his shell. Felix told the vet, Dr. Moreau, who came that afternoon. She cleaned the crack and covered it with a patch.
qs: What did the children feed Gorm?

stories.text: Aisha Bello drove a delivery van for a furniture company in Lagos. On Monday she had to bring a sofa to a house on Marina Road. The sofa was too wide for the door, so Aisha and the owner took the legs off. Then they carried it inside without trouble. The owner, Mr. Eze, gave her a cold drink before she left.
qs: What did Aisha have to deliver?
Why did they take the legs off?
the sofa was too wide for the door
Who gave Aisha a cold drink?

stories.text: Nadia Petrova ran a small flower stall at the corner of Lenin Square. Every morning at six she bought roses from a grower named Ivan. On Valentine's Day she sold three hundred roses before lunch. A young man bought the last rose for his girlfriend, Katya. Nadia closed the stall early and went home to sleep.
qs: Who did Nadia buy roses from?
How many roses did Nadia sell before lunch?
Who was the last rose for?
What did Nadia buy every morning?

stories.text: Rahul lost his blue backpack on the bus to Delhi. Inside it were his passport and a camera. The driver, Mr. Singh, found the backpack under a seat at the last stop. He took it to the bus office, where Rahul picked it up the next day. Rahul gave Mr. Singh a box of sweets to say thank you.
qs: Where did Mr. Singh find the backpack?
Where did Mr. Singh take the backpack?
What did Rahul give Mr. Singh?

stories.text: Two crows, Kaa and Mott, lived in the tall oak beside the mill. Kaa was clever, and Mott was strong. One autumn they found a walnut that was too hard to crack. Mott dropped it on the stones of the road, but it did not break. Kaa waited until a cart rolled over it, and then they shared the nut.
qs: in the tall oak beside the mill

stories.text: Fatima Zahra worked at a hotel in Marrakech. At eight o'clock on Friday evening a family of five arrived without a booking. The hotel was nearly full, but Fatima found them two rooms on the third floor. The father, Mr. Duval, was very grateful. The next morning he left a thank-you card at the front desk.
qs: at eight o'clock on friday evening
How many rooms did Fatima find?
What did Mr. Duval leave at the front desk?

stories.text: Liam's grandmother lived alone in a stone cottage in the hills of Wales. Every Sunday Liam cycled out to visit her. He brought bread and milk from the shop in the village. One Sunday he found her kitchen tap leaking, so he fixed it with a new washer. She made him tea and gave him a slice of apple cake.
qs: Whose grandmother lived in the cottage?
in a stone cottage in the hills of wales
What did the grandmother give Liam?

stories.text: At the harbor in Valparaiso, a fisherman named Pedro mended his nets every afternoon. A seagull called Gris always waited on the post beside him. Pedro threw Gris the small fish that were too little to sell. One day a tourist tried to feed Gris a cracker, but the bird flew away. Gris only trusted Pedro.
qs: Where did Pedro mend his nets?
What did Pedro throw to Gris?
What did the tourist try to feed Gris?

stories.text: Mei Ling and her father opened a noodle shop on Hill Road in March. On the first day only six customers came. Mei Ling painted a bright sign and hung it above the door. By the end of April the shop was full every night. Her father said the sign had brought them luck.
qs: Who opened the noodle shop with her father?
When did they open the shop?
How many customers came on the first day?

stories.text: Jonas Weber taught music at a school in Hamburg. On Wednesday his violin string broke during a lesson. A student named Greta lent him a spare string from her case. Jonas fixed the violin and finished the lesson. After class he bought Greta a new packet of strings at the music shop.
qs: Who lent Jonas a spare string?
Where did Jonas buy the new strings?

stories.text: Abebe walked his family's three donkeys to the market in Gondar each week. The donkeys carried sacks of coffee beans. On the way he met his friend Selam, who was carrying a heavy jar of oil. Abebe put the jar on the smallest donkey so that Selam could rest. At the market they sold everything and walked home together at sunset.
qs: How many donkeys did Abebe walk to the market?
Who did Abebe meet on the way?
Why did Abebe put the jar on the smallest donkey?

stories.text: Carmen Ruiz worked in an office in Madrid. Every day she ate lunch on a bench in Retiro Park. On Tuesday a pigeon stole half of her sandwich. Her coworker, Pablo, laughed so hard that he spilled his coffee. The next day Carmen brought two sandwiches, one for herself and one for the pigeons.
qs: Who worked in an office in Madrid?
on a bench in retiro park
Why did Carmen bring two sandwiches?
one for herself and one for the pigeons

stories.text: Old Mr. Nakamura grew rice in a valley north of Kyoto. In June heavy rain flooded the lowest field. His grandson Daichi came from the city to help him. Together they dug a ditch to carry the water to the stream. By Friday the field was dry again.
qs: Where did Mr. Nakamura grow rice?
in a valley north of kyoto
Who came from the city to help?
When was the field dry again?

stories.text: Sofia found a small gray kitten under her porch one rainy night. She wrapped it in a towel and gave it warm milk. The next day she took it to her neighbor, Mrs. Novak, who knew a lot about cats. Mrs. Novak said the kitten was about six weeks old. Sofia named it Smoke and kept it.
qs: Where did Sofia find the kitten?
What did Sofia wrap the kitten in?
Who knew a lot about cats?
What did Sofia name the kitten?

stories.text: Kwame was the captain of the football team at his school in Kumasi. Before the final match his boots fell apart. His teammate Kofi lent him an old pair that were one size too big. Kwame stuffed paper into the toes and played anyway. He scored the winning goal in the last minute.
qs: Who was the captain of the football team?
What fell apart before the final match?
Who lent Kwame a pair of boots?
What did Kwame stuff into the toes?

stories.text: The lighthouse keeper, Agnes Moore, lived on a rocky island off the coast of Maine. Each evening at dusk she climbed ninety steps to light the lamp. One foggy night she heard a horn from a small boat. Agnes rang the bell again and again until the boat turned away from the rocks. In the morning the boat's captain rowed over with a sack of potatoes for her.
qs: on a rocky island off the coast of maine
When did Agnes light the lamp?
Who rowed over with a sack of potatoes?

stories.text: Diego's uncle owned an old red truck. On Saturday Diego borrowed the truck to move his sister Ana to a new apartment. They loaded a bed, a table, and four chairs. Halfway across town the truck ran out of fuel. Ana walked to a gas station and came back with a can of gasoline.
qs: Who did Diego help to move?
What did they load into the truck?
a bed, a table, and four chairs
What did Ana come back with?

stories.text: Every Thursday the people of Ballymore met in the church hall to play cards. Mrs. Flynn always brought scones, and Mr. Doyle brought tea. One week the heater in the hall stopped working. Father Kelly carried in a small stove from the priest's house. They played until ten o'clock, warm and happy.
qs: Where did the people of Ballymore meet?
Who carried in a small stove?

stories.text: Zara Ahmed was training for a race in Karachi. She ran along the beach every morning before work. One day she twisted her ankle on a rock. A man selling coconuts helped her to a bench and gave her ice from his cart. Zara rested for a week and still finished the race in March.
qs: Who was training for a race?
Where did Zara run every morning?
Who helped Zara to a bench?
What did the man give Zara?

stories.text: Hamid ran a tea house beside the bridge in Herat. At four o'clock each afternoon the same three old men came in to play chess. One day the youngest of them, Rahim, brought his grandson to watch. The boy beat all three men in a single afternoon. Hamid gave the boy a free cup of tea.
qs: When did the old men come in?
What did the old men play?
What did Hamid give the boy?

stories.text: A hedgehog named Burr slept through the winter in a pile of leaves behind the barn. In April a farmer named Joe began to clear the leaves with a rake. He stopped when he saw Burr curled into a ball. Joe carried the hedgehog to the hedge at the end of the field. Burr woke up there a week later and went looking for beetles.
qs: Who slept in the pile of leaves?
Where was the pile of leaves?
Who began to clear the leaves?
Where did Joe carry the hedgehog?
to the hedge at the end of the field
the hedge at the end of the field
What did Burr go looking for?

stories.text: Anna Kowalski was a pharmacist in Krakow. Late on Saturday a worried father came in because his baby had a fever. Anna gave him medicine and showed him how much to use. She also wrote her phone number on the box. The father called on Sunday to say the baby was much better.
qs: Why did the father come in?
What did Anna write on the box?
What did Anna give the father?

stories.text: Tomasz and his friend Eva planned to climb a mountain near Zakopane. They left the hut at five in the morning. Halfway up, clouds rolled in and it started to snow. Eva wanted to go on, but Tomasz said it was too dangerous. They turned back and drank hot chocolate in the hut instead.
qs: Who planned to climb the mountain with Tomasz?
When did they leave the hut?
What did they drink in the hut?

stories.text: Grace Mwangi sold second-hand books from a wooden cart in Nairobi. A schoolboy named Otieno came by every day but never had money. One day Grace gave him a book of maps and told him to bring it back when he finished. He returned it a week later and could name every river in Africa. Grace gave him a second book about the stars.
qs: What did Grace give Otieno first?
What was the second book about?
from a wooden cart in nairobi

stories.text: Pierre's cello was too heavy for him to carry to the concert hall in Lyon. His friend Marc offered to drive it there in his small car. The cello took up the whole back seat, so Pierre took the bus and met Marc at the hall. The concert began at eight o'clock. Afterward, Marc drove the cello home again.
qs: Whose cello was too heavy to carry?
Who offered to drive the cello?
What did Pierre take to the hall?

stories.text: Ravi kept bees in five wooden hives behind his house. In July he collected forty jars of honey. He gave ten jars to his sister Meera, who sold them at her shop. The rest he kept for his family and friends. Meera said her customers loved the honey because it tasted of mango flowers.
qs: How many jars of honey did Ravi collect?
Who did Ravi give ten jars to?
Why did the customers love the honey?
What did Ravi keep the bees in?

stories.text: Olga's sewing machine stopped working the night before her daughter's wedding. She still had to finish the hem of the dress. Her neighbor Boris brought over his mother's old machine. Olga sewed until midnight and finished the dress. At the wedding everyone said the dress was beautiful.
qs: What did Olga still have to finish?
What did everyone say was beautiful?
